solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: A word from Trump: "Eff off when the old fellah's around"

indicators.note: something that has gone off is spoiled, so its letters are knocked out of their order
to be around something is to surround it, so one piece sits on either side of another

blocks.note: cove is an old-fashioned British slang word for a man or chap
the letter F spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: Trump is quoted swearing at someone to go away whenever an old boy turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'eff off' looks like a censored oath but splits into fodder and signal; the scrambled letters then sit inside COVE. COVFEFE is the garbled word Trump tweeted in 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: Covfefe was a nonsense coinage in a late-night 2017 presidential tweet, so it is literally a term originating with him.

clue.text: see 26ac.
Non-PC French supporters: they're hard to stomach

blocks.note: Frogs is an offensive British nickname for the French, hence the warning that it is not politically correct
legs support the body

explanation.surface: French people who back something are rudely described as unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans or backers, but here they are the limbs that hold a body up.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs' legs are a French delicacy that many diners find too off-putting to eat, so they are a dish people struggle to swallow.

clue.text: Holy man just needs to hold tip of prick

indicators.note: a tip is an extreme end, here the final letter of the word that follows
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: just and fair both mean impartial
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crude remark that a holy man has only to grasp the end of a penis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' feels like the start of a word, but here it is the far end, the last letter. 'Just' is not 'only' but the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu religious ascetic who lives on alms, a kind of holy man.

clue.text: It offers mental relief from personal problem after lay

indicators.note: coming after means following in sequence, so the first-named piece is written second

blocks.note: to lay something down is to place it
BO is body odour, a classic personal hygiene problem

explanation.surface: Something eases the mind of a person whose private trouble follows sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' reads as a sexual encounter, but it is the verb meaning put down. BO is short for body odour, which advertisers used to call a personal problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert pill whose benefit comes only from the patient believing in it, so its comfort is psychological.

clue.text: Randy, ruined by Hello curse,  left out

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are rearranged
out means removed or excluded, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: the two words taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone named Randy has been ruined by Hello magazine's jinx and left out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Randy' looks like a name, but it is the definition. One of the two Ls goes, then the rest is rearranged. Hello! is a British celebrity magazine said to curse the couples it features.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is informal British for sexually eager, and lecherous describes someone with excessive, lustful sexual desire.

clue.text: Craved by petrol-head dieters?

blocks.note: surface reading: the foods that people on a diet long for but must give up
setter's reading: a car enthusiast covets carburettors, which share the same short informal name as carbohydrates

explanation.walkthrough: The short form serves both carburettors, loved by car fanatics, and carbohydrates, craved by dieters; the question mark flags the play on the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped plural is slang for both carburettors in an engine and starchy carbohydrate foods such as bread and pasta.

clue.text: Snub oaf getting erection at bed-time

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting something stands it upright, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a yob is a British slang word for a loutish young man
a cot is a small bed
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone cold-shoulders an idiot who becomes aroused at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' is the Private Eye smut, but in a down answer raising a word turns it upside down. Yob is British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to refuse dealings with a person, firm or event, a deliberate collective cold shoulder.

clue.text: Briefly united, getting head, one on one – bliss!

blocks.note: U is a short form of united, as in football club names
the head of something is its top
I is the Roman numeral one, placed above the next piece in this down entry
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A couple, briefly joined and enjoying oral sex together, are in ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting head' and 'one on one' paint a sexual scene, but they are TOP and two separate ones, I and A, stacked in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect place or state, a paradise of complete happiness, so it stands for perfect contentment.

clue.text: Eye holder welcomes publicity – "It's got teeth"

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the eye sits in its socket in the skull
PR is public relations, ie publicity

explanation.surface: A Private Eye holder enjoys the attention and boasts that the magazine has bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' tempts the reader to think of the magazine, but it is the body part whose holder is the socket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket is a wheel or cog with projecting points that engage a chain or film perforations, so it has teeth.

clue.text: see 14ac.
(& 24dn.) Wally and wife spiking father's piss

indicators.note: to spike a drink is to slip something into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: pater is Latin for father, used in old-fashioned British public-school slang
a wally is British slang for a fool, as is an ass
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An idiot and his wife lace Dad's drink, which is described as piss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss' looks like a rude verdict on the drink, but it is the definition. 'Father's' reads as possessive, yet the 's is 'is' joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing water is the polite euphemism for urinating, and piss is the vulgar verb for the same act.

clue.text: Strict control on Sun and Mail, etc? No one's backing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: re means on the subject of, as in letter headings
the Sun and the Mail are British tabloid newspapers, part of the press
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tight regulation of the tabloids is proposed, but nobody supports it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No one's backing' reads as a lack of support, but 'no' and 'one' are letters to be turned round, with 's as 'is'. The Sun and Daily Mail are British tabloids.
explanation.definitionFit: Repression is the forcible restraint or subjugation of people or speech, a regime of tight, harsh authority.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Chump almost snapped "Be my crony, 'PM in waiting'"

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something snapped is broken, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a jerk is a chump, short of its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool snaps at someone, demanding they become a pal of the would-be prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped' reads as spoke sharply, but it breaks the letters. In 2017 Corbyn led the Labour opposition and was presented as a prime minister in waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: As Leader of the Opposition, Corbyn was the person expected to take over government if Labour won, a premier awaiting office.

clue.text: Tony messed with EU aim – "Whatever you want"

indicators.note: to mess with something is to tamper and disorder it, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair interfered with Europe's goals, offering to do anything they liked.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony suggests Tony Blair and Europe, but both names are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom offers any choice at all, inviting someone to state any item they wish and promising it will be available.

clue.text: Disloyal type, one completely flattened, having dismissed two Republicans

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so letters are removed

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
prostrate means lying flat; both of its Rs are removed
R is the abbreviation for Republican, so two of them is a pair of Rs

explanation.surface: A traitor has been knocked flat after sacking a couple of Republican colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two Republicans' sounds like American politics, but it is just two Rs taken out of PROSTRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a religion, party or principle, a renegade who has deserted former allegiances.

clue.text: Tories oddly placed before publicity factory's routine drudgery

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept
being put in front means coming first in the line of pieces

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
an ad is a piece of publicity
a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

explanation.surface: Conservatives awkwardly put in front of a spin factory face monotonous toil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factory's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking wordplay to definition. 'Publicity factory' suggests a PR firm but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any tedious, repetitive job or way of life with no progress, after the prison wheel turned endlessly by walking.

clue.text: Keen to bonk sexy type

blocks.note: being hot on something is being keen
bonk and stuff are both British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to have sex with an attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a single sentence of desire, but 'to' just joins two words, each giving half the answer. Bonk is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot stuff is an informal term for a person considered very attractive and desirable, a sizzling looker.

clue.text: Admit Environment Secretary half started with a line that helps opponents

definitions.note: a relative clause describing the answer rather than a noun

indicators.note: only the half that starts the word is kept, so the back end is cut away

blocks.note: to own up is to admit
Michael Gove was the UK Environment Secretary in 2017; the front half of his surname
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that the minister half began with a policy line that only helped his rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was the UK Environment Secretary in 2017; only the first half of his surname is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal is a goal scored accidentally against your own side, so it benefits the other team; figuratively any self-inflicted blunder.

clue.text: Carp about being elected, getting wind up?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: a carp is a kind of fish
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: Someone complains about winning a seat and gets nervous or annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the verb to complain, but it is the fish. 'Wind up' suggests annoying someone, but here it means bring to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting or business is to bring it to its end, conclude it.

clue.text: Badly teased, energy gone, May ultimately is "Stable"

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so the letters end up in the wrong order
gone means departed, so that letter is removed
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter counts

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Mocked and exhausted, Theresa May insists that she is 'strong and stable'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote recalls Theresa May's 2017 election slogan 'strong and stable'. One E of the first word goes before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and stable are synonyms, both meaning firmly fixed and not liable to wobble or give way.

clue.text: Lower the worth of powerless DUP? Leave off!

indicators.note: without power means the letter standing for power is removed
off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to undermine the Northern Irish party now it has no clout, and is told to back off.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics symbol for power. The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, which propped up Theresa May's government in 2017; 'Leave' also nods to Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: To devalue is to reduce the value or esteem of something, so it means making it count for less.

clue.text: On that dawn, getting screwed, etc.

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone had sex at daybreak, and so on, the details trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed' gives the usual Private Eye innuendo, but it is the signal to twist the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: And what not is an informal tail phrase meaning and other similar things, exactly what the abbreviation et cetera stands for.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Maybe King Edward, however, rejected Brenda

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: however and but are both conjunctions of contrast
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A royal story: perhaps King Edward was, after all, spurned by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward suggests a monarch, but it is a variety of potato. Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for the Queen, giving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, and a potato is a tuber, so the king is one example; hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Eve faced poo spattering – not Trump's kind of bird

indicators.note: spattering splashes things about in a mess, so the letters are scattered into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eve was confronted with a splattering of excrement from a bird Trump would dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird droppings in the surface tempt the solver to think 'spattering' describes the poo, but it is the signal to rearrange the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove carrying an olive branch symbolises peace, the opposite of a political hawk, which Trump was portrayed as.

clue.text: Labour's leader: love, hate, uncontrolled hate

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter is taken
something uncontrolled runs wild, so its letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the first letter of the party name
love is a score of nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Jeremy Corbyn inspires love and hatred, and in some quarters wild hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of feelings about the Labour leader; only the last word defines. Love as O comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to feel intense disgust or detestation for someone, a stronger synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Lube tits liberally, to provide onscreen help

indicators.note: doing something liberally means freely and without restraint, so the letters are rearranged loosely

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude instruction to oil breasts generously, apparently to help someone watching a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberally' reads as how to apply the lubricant, but it signals rearranging the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtitle a film is to add captions translating or transcribing the dialogue, assisting viewers who read the screen.

clue.text: Short time before second wines?

indicators.note: before means in front of, so the earlier pieces are written first

blocks.note: Clare Short was a Labour cabinet minister, so her first name stands for her surname
T is the abbreviation for time
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A brief pause before a second round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short time' reads as a brief moment, but 'Short' is Clare Short, the Labour politician who resigned from Tony Blair's cabinet over Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, so clarets are a family of French red vintages.

clue.text: NHS bed: stay on yours and don't be stupid

definitions.text: stay on yours and don't be stupid
definitions.note: a fill-in phrase: 'stay on your trolley' rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a wheeled stretcher on which patients wait in overcrowded hospital corridors

blocks.clueFragment: stay on yours and don't be stupid
blocks.note: second meaning: the British idiom about being off it means mad, so staying on it means keeping your wits

explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, where patients are often left on wheeled stretchers. 'Off your trolley' is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital patients lie on wheeled stretchers when no ward bed is free, and the idiom about losing it uses the same object.
